children: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell discussed the league's next round of media rights deals during a CNBC interview in Melbourne, Australia, where the Los Angeles Rams will play the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night (Friday afternoon local time).

Goodell did not confirm if the league will use an opt-out clause that it can trigger at the end of the 2029-2030 season but noted the next round of negotiations might include reworking game packages to adjust for modern TV consumption habits and the shift to streaming.

"One of the things we’re doing as a league is talking to our partners, talking to future partners, potential partners … and evaluating, should we repackage our current packages? Should we think differently about where we go with those things?" stated Goodell. He noted the option would be incredibly valuable to the NFL as it can evaluate what’s happening in the media landscape to make the best decision for fans and the clubs.
One thing that won't change, according to Goodell, is that 100% of the NFL's games will be available on local broadcast television.
The broadcasters with NFL games this year are CBS

. Out-of-market Sunday afternoon games require NFL Sunday Ticket, which costs $240 for the season for new subscribers, payable as $30 a month over eight months, though returning subscribers pay significantly more if bundled with YouTube TV or as a standalone purchase.
